launch-ut-salt-lake-city-liberty-park.address: 600 Harvey Milk Boulevard, Salt Lake City, UT 84105
launch-ut-salt-lake-city-liberty-park.summary: Salt Lake City's historic 100-acre urban park combines three walking loops, two playground areas, Tracy Aviary, Chase Home Museum, a pond, pool, tennis, courts, pavilions and mature shade.
launch-ut-salt-lake-city-liberty-park.hours: Open daily from 5:00 a.m.-11:00 p.m. Tracy Aviary, pool, tennis center, museum, concessions, rides and programs use separate schedules.
launch-ut-salt-lake-city-liberty-park.parking: Enter the one-way counter-clockwise Constitution Drive loop from 900 South or 1300 South and park near the intended feature. Tracy Aviary has a separate west-side lot; the playgrounds, pool and courts are spread around the park.
launch-ut-salt-lake-city-liberty-park.arrival: Use 600 Harvey Milk Boulevard for a general arrival, then follow the official amenities map. Route directly to Tracy Aviary, Rice Pavilion or another named feature when meeting someone.
launch-ut-salt-lake-city-liberty-park.restrooms: Four restroom locations serve the park. The City currently lists restrooms open, but individual buildings can close for cleaning, winterization or construction.
launch-ut-salt-lake-city-liberty-park.cost: General park, path, playground, lawn and court access is free. Tracy Aviary, pool, tennis, rides, concessions, reservations and programs may charge separately.
launch-ut-salt-lake-city-liberty-park.accessibility: Paved loops, accessible parking and developed facilities provide broad access. Feature-level routes vary; Rotary Play Park is being rebuilt as an inclusive regional playground.
launch-ut-salt-lake-city-liberty-park.dogs: Leashed dogs are welcome in the park. There is no listed fenced off-leash area, and dogs should stay out of playground, pool and building areas unless posted otherwise.
launch-ut-salt-lake-city-liberty-park.family: Rice Pavilion Playground remains the dependable equipment-play option. Rotary Play Park remains under construction with a grand opening announced for September 2026; the pond, aviary, courts and broad lawns remain available.
launch-ut-salt-lake-city-liberty-park.transit: UTA Route 9 serves the north side along 900 South and Route 205 serves the west side along 500 East. Choose the side nearest the feature and check live arrivals.
launch-ut-salt-lake-city-liberty-park.need: Rotary Play Park remains closed for reconstruction with a grand opening announced for September 2026. Do not confuse renderings of its future splash zone with a currently operating splash pad; Liberty Park Pool is separate.

launch-ut-salt-lake-city-sugar-house-par.address: 1330 East 2100 South, Salt Lake City, UT 84106
launch-ut-salt-lake-city-sugar-house-par.summary: A 109-acre city park with a 1.38-mile loop, two playgrounds, three restroom buildings, seven pavilions, fields, courts, Sugar House Pond, Parley's Creek and Trail, gardens and a renowned sledding hill.
launch-ut-salt-lake-city-sugar-house-par.hours: Open daily 7:00 a.m.-10:00 p.m. May-October and 7:00 a.m.-9:00 p.m. November-April.
launch-ut-salt-lake-city-sugar-house-par.parking: The internal road runs one-way counter-clockwise. Use the lot nearest the intended pavilion or playground and keep the inside curb clear for walkers, runners and cyclists.
launch-ut-salt-lake-city-sugar-house-par.arrival: Use 1330 East 2100 South for a general arrival, then follow the park map. Named pavilions are the easiest meeting points for the pond, playgrounds, courts and fields.
launch-ut-salt-lake-city-sugar-house-par.restrooms: Fabian Lakeside restroom is open year-round. Parley's Creek and Hidden Grove restroom buildings close in winter.
launch-ut-salt-lake-city-sugar-house-par.cost: General park, paths, playgrounds, fields and pond overlooks are free. Pavilion and field reservations, permits and special events may charge.
launch-ut-salt-lake-city-sugar-house-par.accessibility: The paved inner lane loops 1.38 miles with about 92 feet of elevation gain. Developed pavilions, playgrounds and lots have firm approaches, while grass slopes and snow vary.
launch-ut-salt-lake-city-sugar-house-par.dogs: Dogs must remain leashed and controlled everywhere in Sugar House Park; there is no off-leash area.
launch-ut-salt-lake-city-sugar-house-par.family: Parley's Creek and Sugar Beet playgrounds serve different sides of the park. The pond and creek are not swimming or splash areas, and water entry is prohibited.
launch-ut-salt-lake-city-sugar-house-par.transit: UTA Route 21 serves 2100 South by the park; Route 220 may suit other approaches. Use live trip planning for the exact pavilion or entrance.
launch-ut-salt-lake-city-sugar-house-par.need: Big Field remains open and continues to host permitted events. The separate Backstop Field is closed for softball construction through 2026; Hidden Grove and Mt. Olympus pavilions are not accepting 2026 reservations, and fireworks are prohibited year-round.

launch-ut-salt-lake-city-memory-grove-pa.address: 300 North Canyon Road, Salt Lake City, UT 84103
launch-ut-salt-lake-city-memory-grove-pa.summary: A historic veterans memorial landscape at the mouth of City Creek Canyon with monuments, lawns, pond, paths, picnic tables and access to the Freedom Trail and Lower City Creek Natural Area.
launch-ut-salt-lake-city-memory-grove-pa.hours: Memory Grove follows posted City park hours. City Creek Canyon is currently open 8:30 a.m.-10:00 p.m., closing at 8:00 p.m. on listed summer holidays; construction can change access.
launch-ut-salt-lake-city-memory-grove-pa.parking: Closest parking is limited. Use legal parking near the lower Canyon Road entrance and walk in; Capitol activity, ceremonies and canyon construction can restrict access.
launch-ut-salt-lake-city-memory-grove-pa.arrival: Use 300 North Canyon Road for the formal memorial park. The Freedom Trail and City Creek Canyon continue north beyond the maintained memorial landscape.
launch-ut-salt-lake-city-memory-grove-pa.restrooms: Salt Lake City lists a restroom and drinking fountain in Memory Grove. Facilities become sparse farther into the natural area and canyon.
launch-ut-salt-lake-city-memory-grove-pa.cost: General memorial park and trail access is free. Permitted ceremonies, reservations and special events may charge.
launch-ut-salt-lake-city-memory-grove-pa.accessibility: The formal park has developed paths, but canyon connections add grade and natural surfaces. Construction traffic and limited close parking can affect step-free arrival.
launch-ut-salt-lake-city-memory-grove-pa.dogs: Dogs must be leashed inside the memorial park. The adjacent half-mile Freedom Trail is designated off leash; dogs are prohibited above City Creek picnic site 16 and must stay out of the creek.
launch-ut-salt-lake-city-memory-grove-pa.family: This is a memorial and walking destination rather than a playground. Keep children close around the pond, creek, monuments, dogs, stairs and shared canyon road.
launch-ut-salt-lake-city-memory-grove-pa.transit: Downtown buses and TRAX can bring visitors near State Street, North Temple or the Capitol, followed by a walk. No regular route enters Memory Grove or the canyon.
launch-ut-salt-lake-city-memory-grove-pa.need: Private vehicles are currently prohibited in City Creek Canyon during construction. People and pets may never enter the water inside Memory Grove, and canyon picnic reservations are paused during the project.

launch-ut-millcreek-millcreek-canyon.summary: A forested Wasatch canyon with year-round hiking, mountain biking, picnicking, winter skiing and snowshoeing, an alternating-day dog and bicycle system, and a seasonal upper road.
launch-ut-millcreek-millcreek-canyon.hours: The canyon is generally available daily, but the upper winter gate closes every November 1 and road, picnic and trail access changes with snow, storms and maintenance.
launch-ut-millcreek-millcreek-canyon.parking: Small pullouts and trailhead lots fill quickly. Park only in legal designated areas, never block the narrow road, and expect a longer walk when popular Church Fork, Pipeline and Big Water areas fill.
launch-ut-millcreek-millcreek-canyon.arrival: Enter from Wasatch Boulevard at 3800 South and choose a named trailhead before driving uphill. The access fee is collected when leaving the canyon.
launch-ut-millcreek-millcreek-canyon.restrooms: The Forest Service lists no general restroom or potable-water service for the canyon. Some reservable developed sites may have seasonal facilities; arrive self-sufficient.
launch-ut-millcreek-millcreek-canyon.cost: The current canyon use fee is $5 per vehicle, $3 for seniors, with annual canyon passes available. Interagency federal recreation passes are not accepted for this county fee.
launch-ut-millcreek-millcreek-canyon.accessibility: Developed picnic areas and pullouts vary. Most trails are natural-surface routes with roots, rock, snow and significant grade; verify the exact destination before arrival.
launch-ut-millcreek-millcreek-canyon.dogs: Dogs must be leashed canyon-wide on even-numbered days and may be off leash on trails only on odd-numbered days. They remain leashed every day in roads, parking lots, picnic grounds and residential areas.
launch-ut-millcreek-millcreek-canyon.family: Short creekside stops and picnic areas can suit families, but there is no dependable water or general restroom service. Trails, traffic, snow and cold creek water require close supervision.
launch-ut-millcreek-millcreek-canyon.transit: Regular transit does not provide a practical trip through the canyon. Arrange a vehicle and return plan; mobile service can weaken uphill.
launch-ut-millcreek-millcreek-canyon.need: Bicycles are permitted on upper-canyon trails only on even-numbered days, while dog rules favor odd-numbered days. The upper gate closes November 1 and becomes a groomed winter route.

launch-ut-cottonwood-heights-big-cottonw.address: Big Cottonwood Canyon Road and Wasatch Boulevard, Cottonwood Heights, UT 84121
launch-ut-cottonwood-heights-big-cottonw.summary: A major Wasatch watershed canyon along SR-190 with waterfalls, picnic areas, alpine lakes, trailheads, Brighton and Solitude, summer hiking and winter resort access.
launch-ut-cottonwood-heights-big-cottonw.hours: The canyon road is normally open continuously, but avalanche control, crashes, weather, wildfire and maintenance can close or restrict it without a fixed schedule. Individual sites are seasonal.
launch-ut-cottonwood-heights-big-cottonw.parking: Trailhead lots are small and roadside parking is tightly controlled. Choose a named destination, obey no-parking zones and check UDOT traffic before entering; Donut Falls and Silver Lake are frequent pinch points.
launch-ut-cottonwood-heights-big-cottonw.arrival: Enter SR-190 from Wasatch Boulevard and route to the exact trailhead, picnic site or resort. The canyon is long, and a generic pin may leave visitors miles from the intended stop.
launch-ut-cottonwood-heights-big-cottonw.restrooms: Restrooms are available at selected developed picnic sites, visitor facilities and resorts, not at every pullout or trailhead. Carry water and do not drink untreated watershed water.
launch-ut-cottonwood-heights-big-cottonw.cost: Driving the state road and hiking most public trails is free. Picnic reservations, resort activities, parking programs and special facilities may charge separately.
launch-ut-cottonwood-heights-big-cottonw.accessibility: Silver Lake and developed facilities offer some of the strongest accessible options. Most trail routes are rocky, steep and snow-covered seasonally.
launch-ut-cottonwood-heights-big-cottonw.dogs: No pets are allowed anywhere in Big Cottonwood Canyon's protected watershed, including inside vehicles. Qualified service-animal rules are narrower and should be confirmed before arrival.
launch-ut-cottonwood-heights-big-cottonw.family: Silver Lake's boardwalk and short waterfall approaches can work well for families. Fast traffic, cold streams, wildlife and steep unprotected terrain require close supervision.
launch-ut-cottonwood-heights-big-cottonw.transit: Seasonal UTA ski buses and resort transportation vary by year. Outside active service, a compliant vehicle or arranged shuttle is necessary; confirm the return before relying on rideshare.
launch-ut-cottonwood-heights-big-cottonw.need: Winter traction restrictions on SR-190 can require approved tires or chains before snow begins. Check UDOT road status, avalanche control and canyon alerts immediately before leaving.

launch-ut-alta-little-cottonwood-canyon.address: Little Cottonwood Canyon Road and Wasatch Boulevard, Cottonwood Heights, UT 84092
launch-ut-alta-little-cottonwood-canyon.summary: A steep protected watershed canyon along SR-210 with granite history, waterfalls, alpine-lake trails, Snowbird, Alta and seasonal Albion Basin access.
launch-ut-alta-little-cottonwood-canyon.hours: SR-210 is normally open continuously, but avalanche mitigation, storms, crashes, wildfire and construction can close or restrict the canyon. Trailheads and Albion Basin use seasonal schedules.
launch-ut-alta-little-cottonwood-canyon.parking: Parking is scarce at roadside trailheads and resorts. Route to a named destination, obey all no-parking and tow zones, and expect road closures or full lots during powder days and peak summer weekends.
launch-ut-alta-little-cottonwood-canyon.arrival: Enter SR-210 from Wasatch Boulevard and use the exact trailhead, Snowbird or Alta endpoint. Do not use a center-of-canyon pin for White Pine, Temple Quarry or Albion Basin.
launch-ut-alta-little-cottonwood-canyon.restrooms: Dependable restrooms are concentrated at resort and developed sites. Small trailheads may have none; carry water and never drink untreated watershed water.
launch-ut-alta-little-cottonwood-canyon.cost: Public road and most trail access is free. Resort parking and activities, Albion Basin summer access, shuttles and special facilities can carry separate fees.
launch-ut-alta-little-cottonwood-canyon.accessibility: Developed Snowbird and Alta areas provide paved access, while most canyon trails are steep, rocky and snowy. Temple Quarry offers a shorter developed historical route.
launch-ut-alta-little-cottonwood-canyon.dogs: No pets are allowed anywhere in Little Cottonwood Canyon's protected watershed, including in vehicles. Confirm qualified service-animal requirements before travel.
launch-ut-alta-little-cottonwood-canyon.family: Temple Quarry, Lisa Falls and developed resort areas can suit shorter family visits. Streams, granite slabs, traffic, altitude and rapidly changing weather demand close supervision.
launch-ut-alta-little-cottonwood-canyon.transit: Seasonal ski bus and resort service varies. Confirm the current UTA and resort schedule rather than assuming year-round service, and never rely on an uncertain canyon rideshare pickup.
launch-ut-alta-little-cottonwood-canyon.need: SR-210 is highly avalanche-exposed and can close for hours during mitigation. Winter traction rules are strict; summer Albion Basin access and parking can also be controlled.

launch-ut-syracuse-antelope-island-state.summary: A causeway-accessed Great Salt Lake island with beaches, free-ranging bison, desert trails, birding, dark skies, camping and the historic Fielding Garr Ranch.
launch-ut-syracuse-antelope-island-state.hours: Open daily 6:00 a.m.-10:00 p.m. Visitor information operates 9:00 a.m.-5:00 p.m.; Fielding Garr Ranch facilities operate daily 10:00 a.m.-5:00 p.m.
launch-ut-syracuse-antelope-island-state.parking: Drive across the Davis County causeway and use the lot at the specific beach, trailhead, marina or ranch. Distances are substantial and there is no internal public shuttle.
launch-ut-syracuse-antelope-island-state.arrival: Use the official Syracuse entrance and causeway. Rideshare operators do not pick up in the park, so arriving without a vehicle can leave visitors stranded.
launch-ut-syracuse-antelope-island-state.restrooms: Flush toilets and showers are at Bridger Bay Beach; the marina visitor-information area and developed sites have additional facilities. Remote trails and primitive camps rely on pit toilets or none.
launch-ut-syracuse-antelope-island-state.cost: A state-park day-use fee is charged by vehicle, motorcycle, bicycle or walk-in admission. Confirm the current amount on the official fee page or entrance station before arrival.
launch-ut-syracuse-antelope-island-state.accessibility: The marina information area, developed beach facilities and ranch provide the firmest access. Natural trails, salt shorelines and primitive camps are rough and exposed.
launch-ut-syracuse-antelope-island-state.dogs: Leashed dogs are allowed in many outdoor and camping areas, but wildlife safety and beach/building restrictions apply. Never let a dog approach bison or other wildlife.
launch-ut-syracuse-antelope-island-state.family: Bridger Bay, visitor interpretation and Fielding Garr Ranch can form a strong family day. Carry water, insect protection and sun protection, and keep children far from bison.
launch-ut-syracuse-antelope-island-state.transit: No public transit serves the island and rideshares do not retrieve passengers. Bring a vehicle, fuel, water and a reliable return plan.
launch-ut-syracuse-antelope-island-state.need: The main Visitor Center is closed for renovation; temporary visitor information and gifts are at the marina. Stage 2 fire restrictions are active, and Egg Island and White Rock are closed year-round for nesting birds.

launch-ut-magna-great-salt-lake-state-pa.summary: A developed Great Salt Lake shoreline and marina destination with public viewpoints, boat access, visitor interpretation, camping, birding and expansive sunset views.
launch-ut-magna-great-salt-lake-state-pa.hours: The park is open sunrise to sunset. Summer Visitor Center hours are 11:00 a.m.-7:00 p.m. Monday-Thursday and 9:00 a.m.-8:00 p.m. Friday-Sunday.
launch-ut-magna-great-salt-lake-state-pa.parking: Use the entrance station and park near the visitor center, marina, campground or Sunset Beach. Black Rock uses a separate trailhead and a walk of a little over one-quarter mile.
launch-ut-magna-great-salt-lake-state-pa.arrival: Navigate to Great Salt Lake State Park in Magna, not a generic Great Salt Lake pin. The lake spans a huge region and other shoreline access points are not interchangeable.
launch-ut-magna-great-salt-lake-state-pa.restrooms: Flush restrooms serve the developed park. Showers are limited to registered campers and marina slip renters using a check-in code.
launch-ut-magna-great-salt-lake-state-pa.cost: Day use is $10 per vehicle up to eight people, $5 for senior vehicles, and $2 per pedestrian or bicyclist. Camping, tours, slips and permits cost separately.
launch-ut-magna-great-salt-lake-state-pa.accessibility: The visitor center, marina and developed viewpoints have firm routes. Low water can move the shoreline far from developed access and create mud or uneven salt crust.
launch-ut-magna-great-salt-lake-state-pa.dogs: Leashed pets are generally allowed in outdoor areas under state-park rules. Keep them out of sensitive bird habitat, marina operations and unsafe shoreline mud.
launch-ut-magna-great-salt-lake-state-pa.family: Visitor exhibits, boats and sunset overlooks are useful with children, but the beach is not a managed swim facility. Supervise closely around docks, steep ramps, mud and salt water.
launch-ut-magna-great-salt-lake-state-pa.transit: Regular transit does not provide a practical trip to the marina. Drive or arrange a confirmed round trip; mobile service and rideshare availability can vary.
launch-ut-magna-great-salt-lake-state-pa.need: Lake levels are low and shoreline conditions change. Stage 2 fire restrictions are active; check current water, algae, wind and marina conditions before boating or walking onto exposed lakebed.
